transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Start: 14:00 PDT | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Lena Park (NovaCrest), Jonas Meyer (NovaCrest), Ravi Kapoor (NovaCrest), Sofia Ortiz (NovaCrest)

Auto-generated summary: Quarterly check-in; focus on cost and latency spikes, pilot scoping for Dedicated capacity, security documents requested.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, um, and then agenda — cost trends, latency, pilot scope, and security questions. Diego will run through the perf options.
[00:18] Lena Park: Hi, thanks. Happy to be here. We've got a couple people from infra and product as well.
[00:23] Jonas Meyer: Hey all, Jonas here. We'll be brief — mostly listening for any infra constraints.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Great. Diego, you want to kick off with what we saw in the last 6 weeks?
[00:33] Diego Alvarez: Yeah. So quick context, NovaCrest's overall token volume is up about 38% month-over-month. Most of the spend delta is embeddings for product recommendations — we think it's the vector refresh cadence. On our side, we looked at the call traces: median latency's fine, around 120ms, but p95 in the busy window (18:00-20:00 ET) has drifted from ~290ms to ~420ms. There's also a small number of tail outliers at the 99th percentile hitting near 1.2s on some requests.
[01:07] Ravi Kapoor: Hmm, that aligns with what we saw on the infra. During catalog reindex, background batch jobs overlap with live traffic which creates bursts. We're on a VPC with NAT egress constraints and some firewall rules that add jitter.
[01:18] Diego Alvarez: Right, two levers we recommended: one is smarter prefix/KV caching so we avoid recomputing embeddings for stable catalog items; second is moving heavier workloads to Dedicated capacity where throughput and steady-state latency are more predictable. Also batching and dynamic quantization profiles can cut token compute by 1.7-2x for your common prompt shapes.
[01:41] Sofia Ortiz: Can you explain the KV thing? I've seen references to K V cash in the notes and I'm not sure if that's the same as a cache?
[01:46] Diego Alvarez: Sorry, yeah, that's the K V cache — key value cache for the model's KV states, and also we mean prefix caching for embeddings. The transcript auto had it as "K V cash" earlier, haha. The idea is you avoid recomputing embeddings if the inputs haven't materially changed.
[02:01] Maya Chen: We also flagged model choice as a cost lever. If you can tolerate a slightly laxer generation quality for recommendations, a quantized open model variant or a smaller transformer reduces per-token cost. We'll run a regression check on your three representative prompts.
[02:15] Lena Park: Quality is important — we need conversion rate parity within 1-2% otherwise business will push back.
[02:21] Diego Alvarez: Totally. So pilot plan: two-week benchmark with a simulated traffic pattern, run on Redwood Dedicated (we'll provision a small pool) vs Hosted (your current setup) and compare cost-per-1000-requests, p95 latency, and tail errors.
[02:37] Jonas Meyer: On the Dedicated note, what's the security story? We have to keep PII out and use our KMS for key management. Also, can the control plane be VPC-private? We heard earlier about a "private deployment" option.
[02:49] Priya Singh: Yes, NovaCrest — we can provide a Private deployment option that gives you a customer-managed control plane and VPC peering. For KMS, we support bring-your-own keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations. We'll attach the SOC2 artifact and the architecture diagram after the call.
[03:05] Ravi Kapoor: When you say "attach the SOC2 artifact" — is that the cert PDF or the full report? We need something our security team can ingest.
[03:11] Priya Singh: We'll send the cert plus a redacted bridge letter and an implementation summary. If you need the full report, we can start an NDA process.
[03:20] Lena Park: That would be fine — the summary and KMS integration notes should unblock us for the initial pilot.
[03:26] Diego Alvarez: For benchmarks, we want to capture the request distribution — short prompts vs embedding refreshes — and emulate bursts. Diego: (laughs) Sorry, I mean, we'll share a harness.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Small note — cost spikes correlate with your embedding refresh cadence. If you move to a change-only refresh (delta updates) you'll probably see token volume drop 25-40%.
[03:45] Sofia Ortiz: Can we do that without re-architecting the entire pipeline?
[03:49] Diego Alvarez: Yes, typically you can add a change log feed that triggers embedding updates only for changed SKUs. We can share design patterns.
[03:56] Jonas Meyer: Another question on SLA: what's typical p95 guarantee on Dedicated?
[04:02] Maya Chen: Our Dedicated commitments for similar customers have a p95 latency target around 250-350ms for typical gen calls, but it depends on model, sequence length, and the capacity config. We'll provide a profile based on the model/seq-lengths you give us.
[04:18] Lena Park: Sequence lengths vary but for embeddings it's basically fixed small tokens ~128, for recommendation prompts average 220 tokens.
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: Good. That helps. Also, we noticed a small number of retried requests — about 0.6% — which disproportionately drove tail latency. We recommend idempotency keys and a short retry-backoff policy to reduce duplicates.
[04:40] Ravi Kapoor: Noted. On the networking side, we'll need to test egress throughput and connection churn during peak reindexing. That may surface NAT saturation which we haven't fully instrumented.
[04:50] Diego Alvarez: We can help run a small chaos test during the benchmark to simulate that.
[04:54] Maya Chen: Quick pause to check time — we've covered a lot. Any blockers we haven't addressed?
[04:59] Lena Park: The main blocker is cost forecasting. Can you show us a token-level cost forecast that ties into our billing cadence? We need to show finance.
[05:07] Maya Chen: Yes, action: I'll share a token-level cost sheet and annotate where most of the spend is coming from. We'll include a scenario with delta updates vs full refresh.
[05:14] Jonas Meyer: Also, is there a self-serve way to toggle quantization or batching parameters for Dedicated during the pilot?
[05:20] Diego Alvarez: You can make those adjustments via the Redwood Console — we can give you RBAC access for a sandbox host. For private deployments, some knobs are managed with our ops team, but the Console surfaces suggestions and toggles.
[05:34] Sofia Ortiz: What's the timeline you propose for the pilot? Q4?
[05:37] Priya Singh: If we get the artifacts by next Monday and confirm success metrics, we can plan a two-week benchmark the week of 9/20, and run a constrained pilot through October.
[05:48] Lena Park: That timeline works if we get the security docs quickly.
[05:51] Maya Chen: We'll target sending SOC2 and KMS docs by 9/13.
[05:56] Jonas Meyer: One last question — any recommendations on model selection? We currently use an LLM for both chat and embeddings. Could splitting them reduce cost?
[06:04] Diego Alvarez: Yes, separating embeddings to a smaller, specialized embedder and using a generation-focused model for chat/recs is often cheaper. Embedding ops can use a quantized vector model that is far cheaper per vector. We can run a small eval to show quality delta.
[06:18] Lena Park: Please do. We'll need conversion parity tests as part of the success metrics.
[06:22] Diego Alvarez: Understood. We'll include that in the benchmark.
[06:25] (crosstalk)
[06:30] Maya Chen: Alright — recap and owners: Maya will send cost sheet (due 9/16), Priya sends SOC2 + KMS notes (due 9/13), Diego will propose benchmark harness and load profile (due 9/14), NovaCrest (Lena/Sofia) will pick 3 prompts and metrics (due 9/15). 
[06:48] Ravi Kapoor: We'll also provide the VPC network diagram by 9/14.
[06:53] Maya Chen: Perfect. Any other risks we should call out?
[06:56] Jonas Meyer: Potential risk is catalog reindex cadence — if that stays high we might need a hybrid approach with burst capacity.
[07:04] Diego Alvarez: We can design an autoscale policy that uses a burst pool for scheduled reindexes. That reduces baseline cost.
[07:12] Lena Park: Ok. Thanks — that sounds reasonable.
[07:16] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with times for the benchmark. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end: 14:58 PDT.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Customer emphasized conversion parity requirement for any model/quantization change.
- Security artifacts are gating pilot kickoff.
- Next immediate milestone: cost sheet and SOC2 artifacts in the next 4 business days.

Transcript quirks: occasional mis-transcribed product names and acronyms (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "Dedicate" instead of Dedicated), filler words retained, some speaker labels corrected manually.

Call closed with explicit next steps and owners.
